_description: Timeline of upper bounds on the matrix-multiplication exponent ω, the smallest constant such that ⟨n,n,n⟩ matrix multiplication can be performed in O(n^ω) arithmetic operations as n → ∞. Each entry is the announcement of a new ω upper bound, attributed to its primary paper. The lower bound has been ω ≥ 2 (information-theoretic trivial) since the problem was posed; whether ω = 2 is one of the major open problems in algebraic complexity. Pan's 2014 survey (refs [66] + [67]) gives a comprehensive narrative of the progress.

_schema.year: year of public announcement (preprint or proceedings, whichever first)
_schema.omega_upper: upper bound on ω announced this year

lower_bound_source: information-theoretic (the n² output entries cannot be produced in fewer than n² operations)

entries.notes: log_2(7) ≈ 2.8074. First breach of the cubic barrier. Defied attack for almost a decade.
First post-Strassen improvement. Pan introduced TA in his 1972 Russian paper; the 1978 FOCS paper announces the new ω bound. log_70(143,640) < 2.7962.
First use of approximate (any-precision) algorithms via ε-decompositions: R̃(⟨2,2,3⟩) ≤ 10 vs R(⟨2,2,3⟩) = 11.
Major jump: laser-method-style aggregation of multiple disjoint matmuls.
Cleaner exposition + refinement of Schönhage's framework.
Used the CW tensor; the ⟨2,2,2⟩-anchored exponent that held for ~25 years.
log of the analysis improved another decimal.

entries.method: Refined CW analysis (slight regression in some claims)
entries.notes: Different analysis of the same family.
